description: One episode in full, read out of the index: identity, authorship, message, trailers and the file rows with their taxonomy decisions. Owner: `e1.10`, on the rows `e1.2` stores.

asked.description: The handle the user typed, echoed beside what it resolved to.

identity.description: Which episode this commit belongs to, as the `episode` table knows it: the identity that survives a rewrite, the rule that drew its boundary and how much the tool trusts that rule. Null when the index has no episode for the commit - a store written before episode segmentation, or a commit the walk can no longer reach - because 'not known' and 'weakly known' are different statements (ADR-006 §10.3).

add.description: Added lines across every commit in the episode, not just this one.

attribution.description: The case behind `author_kind` (`e4.1`): the rung that decided, the agent it named, the evidence list, and the reason a label was refused. Null when the row was written before migration 4, which stored the label and nothing else.

agent.description: The agent the evidence named, when it named exactly one.

confidence.description: Confidence in `kind`; 0.0 means nothing was known, not that nothing matters.

evidence.description: Every rung that fired, strongest first.

detail.description: The literal, in the commit's own spelling.

reason.description: Why the verdict is `unknown`, or why a label was refused rather than guessed.

author_confidence.description: `author_kind`'s confidence: a signature is certain, a heuristic is a prior.

boundary_confidence.description: How much the boundary rule that won is trusted; `override` is 1.0 because a human said so.

commits.description: How many commits the episode holds; `members` is the same list.

files.description: Distinct paths the whole episode touched.

fingerprint.description: The episode's own identity digest - author plus sorted touched paths - which is what carries review state across an amend or rebase.

id.description: The episode id, stable across rewrites of its commits.

intent.description: What the episode was *for* (`e4.2`): the ladder that answered it - the harness prompt, a declared intent line, an `Intent:`/`Task:` trailer, a plan item, a prompt digest - with the plan items, the declared scope globs and the evidence list beside it. Null when the row was written before migration 5, which stored no intent at all: a different fact from `state: none`, which means every source was read and none of them stated anything.

confidence.description: Confidence in `text`; 0.0 means nothing was recorded, not that nothing matters.

evidence.description: Every rung that fired, strongest first - including one that exists but is switched off by `[intent] sources`.

detail.description: The literal, in the source's own spelling.

plan.description: The plan items, in the order they were stated; empty when nothing stated a plan.

status.description: The item's state in the harness's own words, when it had one.

prompt.description: The turn's prompt digests, and whether its text came with them. A digest with no text is `state: digest-only`, not an absence - ADR-005's `turn_start` row carries a digest precisely so that rewording a subject line cannot move a corpus digest.

reason.description: What was looked for and not found - the reading that makes `state: none` a checked absence rather than a blank.

schema.description: The document's own namespace, so a reader of the store column knows which shape it holds.

scope.description: The declared scope, as repository-relative path globs, normalised, sorted and deduplicated. The input the scope-creep comparison reads (`fathom_analyze::scope::deviation`); nothing in this build enforces it.

scope_rejected.description: Declared scope values refused rather than quietly dropped: an absolute path, a `..`, a NUL.

session_id.description: The harness session the intent arrived on, when an event or an `Agent-Session:` trailer named one.

state.description: `recorded`, `digest-only` or `none`. The last is a state with a reason, never a blank.

text.description: The request, in the asker's own words. Absent unless `state` is `recorded`.

truncated.description: Whether `text` was cut at the stored byte cap; a quote that stops mid-sentence says so.

turn_id.description: The harness turn the intent arrived on, session-qualified.

lineage_ref.description: `rebase:<branch>` when the episode was relinked across a rewrite.

live.description: False once the episode was rewritten away and only review state keeps it.

members.description: Every commit id in the episode, oldest first.

overridden.description: True when `fathom.toml` forced this boundary; the card says so in words.

session_id.description: Harness session when a transcript event named one.

turn_id.description: Harness turn the episode answers, when known. Session-qualified (`<session_id>:<turn_index>`) whenever a session is known: ADR-003 §9.1 defines the id, and ADR-003 §18.2 D4 is the defect that had the trailer transport carrying the bare index.

turn_index.description: The turn number inside turn_id, derived rather than stored: null when there is no turn, and null when the id carries something that is not a number.

title: fathom show --json

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: OK
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the verb answered, and the index describes HEAD

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: ERROR
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: a rev that names nothing, an unimplemented verb, a rejected argument value

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: USAGE
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: clap rejected the command line (bad flag, unknown verb, missing value)

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: NOT_A_REPOSITORY
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: --root is not a git repository, or `.git` is unreadable

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: STORE_CORRUPT
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the store failed its integrity checks

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: FEATURE_ABSENT
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the verb needs a feature this binary was not built with

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: INDEX_DEGRADED
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the index is missing, stale, incomplete, or a run never closed
